expectations.text: GET /api/fuel response changed to ok({ rows, total }); rows is the existing list shape
expectations.evidence: Line 74: `return ok({ rows, total })`. rows SELECT preserves fr.*, row_to_json(v.*) as vehicles, json_build_object(...) as drivers, ORDER BY fr.fuel_record_id DESC.

expectations.text: total is computed by a COUNT query (not rows.length) honoring the same WHERE filters as the rows query, before LIMIT/OFFSET is applied
expectations.evidence: Lines 70-73: `SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS total ${JOINS} ${where}` via Promise.all with countParams (no pagination appended). Cast to int so it serializes through exec_query RPC.

expectations.text: COUNT query keeps the JOINs to vehicles/drivers/employees so search filters on joined columns (plate_number, employee names) still work
expectations.evidence: COUNT query uses the same JOINS block (lines 41-46) so search conditions on v.plate_number / e.first_name / e.last_name resolve. NOTES.md explains the 1:1 parent joins make COUNT(*) safe.

expectations.text: Existing filters (vehicle_id, driver_id, fuel_type, status, search, from_date, to_date) and pagination (page/pageSize -> LIMIT/OFFSET) preserved
expectations.evidence: All six filter branches preserved; data query clones countParams and appends LIMIT/OFFSET. `status !== 'all'`, ILIKE search, from_date/to_date all intact.

expectations.text: All user input reaches SQL only through $n placeholders
expectations.evidence: All filter values appended to countParams and referenced as $1..$n; params for the data query are a clone of countParams plus LIMIT/OFFSET values.

expectations.text: src/services/fuel.service.js still passes page/pageSize through via buildQuery and works with the new response shape
expectations.evidence: fuel.service.js unchanged; getFuelRecords(filters) -> apiFetch with buildQuery, which passes page/pageSize and returns { rows, total } transparently.

claims.claim: COUNT(*)::int cast avoids bigint JSON serialization issues through exec_query RPC
claims.evidence: Line 72 uses `COUNT(*)::int AS total`; NOTES.md documents the bigint-vs-JSON concern.

claims.claim: Promise.all runs count and rows queries in parallel
claims.evidence: Line 70 destructures `[{ rows }, { rows: [{ total }] }] = await Promise.all([...])`.
